decisions.rationale: 'Lesch-Nyhan' appears in the title only as a modifier of 'locus' (a gene location named after the disease), so it is a disease name used to modify another concept rather than a standalone disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 (Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: 'disease' is a very general term used in 'leading to human disease' and is explicitly excluded, not a specific or class-level disease name.
'Lesch-Nyhan syndrome' refers to one specific, well-defined disease with no further subcategorization, used as the disease whose patients were studied.
In 'Lesch-Nyhan patients' the disease name functions as a modifier of the noun 'patients' rather than naming a disease entity on its own.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 (Modifiers for other concepts)

decisions.rationale: 'Lesch-Nyhan syndrome' in 'cases of Lesch-Nyhan syndrome' refers to one specific disease, so the full phrase is the minimal span for the most specific form.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease) and §5 (Minimum necessary span)
